c. 400 BCE
Hippocratic writings teach that disease has natural causes, not punishment from gods
The Hippocratic Corpus, linked to Hippocrates of Kos, Greece.
c. 162 CE
Galen arrives in Rome and becomes its most famous doctor
His anatomy (much of it from animals) dominated medicine for about 1,400 years.
Vesalius publishes "De humani corporis fabrica"
The first great anatomy atlas based on human dissection, correcting many of Galen's errors.
William Harvey shows blood circulates, pumped by the heart
Published in "De Motu Cordis".
Antonie van Leeuwenhoek reports seeing microbes
He called them "animalcules", seen with his own homemade microscopes.
Edward Jenner tests the first vaccine (cowpox against smallpox)
"Vaccine" comes from vacca, Latin for cow.
René Laennec invents the stethoscope
His first was a rolled-up tube of paper.
First public demonstration of ether anesthesia in surgery
At Massachusetts General Hospital, Boston (William Morton).
Ignaz Semmelweis cuts deaths on a hospital ward with handwashing
Doctors washed in chlorinated lime solution in Vienna; he was ignored for years.
John Snow traces a cholera outbreak to the Broad Street water pump
A founding moment of epidemiology, in London.
Joseph Lister publishes antiseptic surgery with carbolic acid
Deaths after surgery dropped sharply.
Robert Koch identifies the bacterium that causes tuberculosis
Mycobacterium tuberculosis. 24 March is now World TB Day.
Louis Pasteur gives the rabies vaccine to Joseph Meister
The 9-year-old boy survived.
Wilhelm Röntgen discovers X-rays
The first X-ray image showed his wife's hand and ring.
Felix Hoffmann at Bayer makes a pure, stable form of aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid)
Willow bark salicylates had been used for pain since ancient times.
Karl Landsteiner discovers the ABO blood groups
Made safe blood transfusion possible; Nobel Prize 1930.
Willem Einthoven records the ECG with his string galvanometer
He named the P, Q, R, S and T waves. Nobel Prize 1924.
Golgi and Cajal share the Nobel Prize for the structure of the nervous system
Cajal showed neurons are separate cells (the neuron doctrine).
First patient treated with insulin (Leonard Thompson, Toronto)
Discovered by Banting and Best's team in 1921.
Alexander Fleming discovers penicillin
Mould killed bacteria on a plate he left out.
Hans Berger publishes the first human EEG
Recording the brain's electrical waves through the scalp.
Gerhard Domagk publishes the first sulfa antibiotic (Prontosil)
The first widely used synthetic antibacterial drug.
Chlorpromazine, the first antipsychotic, is used in psychiatry
Started in Paris; it transformed mental health care.
Watson and Crick publish the double-helix structure of DNA
Built on Rosalind Franklin's X-ray image "Photo 51".
First successful kidney transplant (between identical twins)
Joseph Murray's team in Boston.
Jonas Salk's polio vaccine is declared safe and effective
Announced on 12 April 1955.
First fully implanted pacemaker (Arne Larsson, Sweden)
He outlived both the inventor and the surgeon.
First human heart transplant (Christiaan Barnard, Cape Town)
The patient lived 18 days.
First CT scan of a patient's brain
Godfrey Hounsfield's scanner found a brain tumour in London.
First MRI scan of a human body
Raymond Damadian's machine "Indomitable".
WHO declares smallpox eradicated
The only human disease wiped out so far.
First statin (lovastatin) approved in the US
Cholesterol lowering for heart disease.
Human Genome Project completed
About 20,000 protein-coding genes mapped.
First mRNA vaccines authorized (COVID-19)
Decades of mRNA research by scientists like Katalin Karikó.
